'''Simon Hugh Piper Maddrell''' [[Fellow of the Royal Society|FRS]]<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Skaer |first1=Helen |last2=O'Donnell |first2=Michael J. |last3=Dow |first3=Julian A. T. |date=2022 |title=Simon Hugh Piper Maddrell. 11 December 1937—10 September 2020 |url=https://royalsocietypublishing.org/doi/10.1098/rsbm.2021.0039 |journal=Biographical Memoirs of Fellows of the Royal Society |volume=73|pages=357–377 |doi=10.1098/rsbm.2021.0039 |s2cid=250093363 |doi-access=free }}</ref> (11 December 1937 – 10 September 2020) was a British [[Insect physiology|insect physiologist]] whose work predominantly focused on insect kidney organs—the [[Malpighian tubule system|Malpighian]] tubules. Based at the Department of Zoology at the [[University of Cambridge]] (where he had gained his undergraduate degree, followed by a PhD), his research involved insects such as ''[[Rhodnius prolixus]]'' and later, ''[[Drosophila melanogaster]].'' At Cambridge he was a fellow of [[Gonville and Caius College, Cambridge|Gonville and Caius College]].

He was associated with [[The Company of Biologists]] for much of his career, including a financial advisory role.<ref>{{Cite web |title=A tribute to Professor Simon Maddrell |url=https://www.biologists.com/stories/a-tribute-to-professor-simon-maddrell/}}</ref>

He was elected Fellow of [[Royal Society|the Royal Society]] in 1981.
